title: VSift speaker labels v1
description: Speaker labels (0.3.0, ADR 0031): the speakers block that transcript.get, search, transcript.speakers and transcript.name-speaker carry, and the per-segment speaker_label. Labels are provisional: S1, S2 and so on group transcript segments the diarization engine heard in one voice, numbered by when each voice is first heard. A label is not who the person is, two similar voices can share one label, and a segment in which two people speak is not split: the labels have segment precision. A verified_name is the user's own statement, never inferred from a voice or the screen. This is distinct from a segment's speaker member, a voice tag of a supplied WebVTT file. No voice-derived vector is ever part of an answer or a stored record.

record_number.description: 1-based number of the record among the session's speaker records: each labelling and each recorded or cleared name commits the next one.

labelling.description: speaker-labels-v1: a segment gets the label that holds at least 70% of the speech the engine heard inside it, when that speech covers at least half of the segment; otherwise it has no confident speaker.

given_speaker_count.description: The speaker count the user gave, passed to the engine as given; null when the engine counted.

diarized_range.description: The source time the engine heard: the whole source, or the range asked for (at most the duration cap).

display.description: How the label reads in a report: 'S2, by voice', or '<name> (S2, named by the user)'.

verified_name.description: The name the user recorded for the label, exactly as given (1 to 128 bytes, no control character); null when none.

coverage.description: Which of the revision's segments have a label, which have no confident speaker, and which lie outside the audio the engine heard; each list is merged, in start order, and cut at 100 ranges (ranges_truncated).

statement.description: Fixed prose saying what a label is and is not.

segment_speaker_label.description: A segment's speaker under the revision's newest speaker record. label is null when no label clearly holds the segment, and no_confident_speaker then says why: little_speech (the engine heard speech in less than half of it) or mixed (no label holds 70% of the speech, often two people).

segment_speaker_label_brief.description: A segment's speaker label in the brief view: the label (null for no confident speaker) and how it reads.

result_data.description: The data member of a transcript.speakers or transcript.name-speaker result: the record it committed. The envelope's status is partial, with a fixed warning, when some segment has no label; it still exits 0.
